method.intro: Each component is normalized to 0–100 with a linear mapping, then combined with fixed weights:
method.trend: Trend momentum ({{w}}%): 30-day growth of active ads, mapped from {{lo}}% → 0 to +{{hi}}% → 100 (7-day growth if 30-day history is missing).
method.ads: Advertising traction ({{w}}%): 60% active-ad volume (log scale, 25+ = 100) and 40% advertiser diversity (1 → 0, 12+ → 100).
method.margin: Estimated gross margin ({{w}}%): (price − supplier cost) / price, mapped from {{lo}}% → 0 to {{hi}}% → 100.
method.competition: Competition & saturation ({{w}}%): 100 − saturation estimate (advertisers and stores observed).
method.differentiation: Differentiation ({{w}}%): analyst estimate of how distinct the product is.
method.freshness: Freshness & evidence ({{w}}%): days since last observation (0 → 100, 30+ → 0) and amount of evidence.
method.missing: Missing components are excluded and weights re-normalized. With fewer than 14 days of observations, fewer than 3 ads, or 2+ missing components, the score is withheld.

calculator.subtitle: Model unit economics with your own assumptions. Results update instantly.

calculator.assumptionsDesc: Per order, in your selected currency

tips.price: Price paid by the customer, excluding taxes you collect.
tips.productCost: Unit cost from your supplier quotation.
tips.shippingCost: Fulfilment and delivery cost per order.
tips.paymentFeePct: Percentage taken by the payment processor.
tips.platformCostPerOrder: Monthly Shopify plan and apps divided by expected orders.
tips.cpa: Average advertising cost to acquire one order.
tips.refundRatePct: Share of revenue you expect to refund.
tips.fixedMonthlyCosts: Costs that do not vary with orders (tools, subscriptions).

def.grossMargin: Price − product cost − shipping − payment fees.
def.contribution: Price − all variable costs per order (incl. platform, refunds, other), before advertising. Equals the break-even CPA.
def.breakEvenCpa: Maximum you can pay in ads per order without losing money on the order.
def.breakEvenRoas: Price ÷ contribution margin. Below this ROAS each order loses money.
def.operatingProfit: Net contribution × orders − fixed monthly costs. Not net profit: taxes, salaries and financing are excluded.
def.breakEvenOrders: Fixed monthly costs ÷ net contribution per order.

calculator.sensitivityDesc: Net contribution per order when price and CPA change
calculator.note1: Contribution margin is not net profit. Net profit also deducts taxes, salaries, financing and one-off costs.
calculator.note2: Estimated product margins in research records are not verified supplier quotations or actual operating results.
calculator.note3: Changing the interface language only changes number formatting, never the calculations.

faq.q1: Where does the data come from?
faq.a1: From connectors to official APIs (such as the Meta Ad Library API), licensed data providers and public storefront pages. The demo uses synthetic data, labelled everywhere.
faq.q2: Does a high score mean a product will sell?
faq.a2: No. The score is a research heuristic to prioritise what to test. Always validate with samples, real quotes and small ad tests.
faq.a3: Not from private analytics — that data is not public. Any estimate would be labelled with its method and confidence, and omitted when evidence is weak.
faq.a4: French, English, Spanish, German and Italian, with dates, numbers and currencies formatted for your locale.
faq.q5: Can I connect my Shopify store?
faq.a5: Yes, on Pro and Business plans, through Shopify OAuth with read-only permissions, to compare your own performance with the market.

legal.template: Template provided for the TrendHunter software. Have it reviewed by legal counsel and completed with your company details before production use.

sections.title: 1. Who we are
sections.body: TrendHunter (“we”) operates the TrendHunter service. The data controller is the company identified in the legal notice of the deployment.

sections.title: 2. Data we collect
sections.body: Account data (name, email), workspace data you create (collections, notes, alerts), usage counters required to enforce plan limits, billing records handled by Stripe, and technical logs for security.

sections.title: 3. Purposes and legal bases
sections.body: Providing the service (contract), securing the platform and preventing abuse (legitimate interest), billing (legal obligation and contract), and optional emails you enable (consent).

sections.title: 4. Research data
sections.body: Market research data comes from official APIs, licensed providers and publicly accessible web pages collected in line with robots policies and site terms. We do not collect private data from other merchants.

sections.title: 5. Processors
sections.body: Hosting, database (Supabase), payments (Stripe), email (Resend) and AI analysis (Anthropic) act as processors under data processing agreements.

sections.title: 6. Retention
sections.body: Account data is kept while your account is active. Usage events are kept up to 13 months. Raw connector payloads are kept for the retention period documented per connector.

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.body: You can access, export and delete your data at any time from Settings → Privacy & data, and contact us to exercise rectification, restriction, objection or portability rights. You may also lodge a complaint with your data protection authority.

sections.title: 8. Cookies
sections.body: We use strictly necessary cookies for authentication, language and security. Analytics or advertising cookies are only set with your consent.

sections.title: 1. Service
sections.body: TrendHunter provides research tools for e-commerce. Information is provided for research purposes and does not constitute financial, legal or business advice.

sections.title: 2. No guarantee of results
sections.body: Opportunity scores, estimates and AI-generated analyses are heuristics. They do not guarantee sales, profitability or any outcome.

sections.title: 3. Acceptable use
sections.body: You must not use the service to infringe intellectual property, copy third-party advertising content verbatim, bypass technical restrictions, or collect personal data unlawfully.

sections.title: 4. Third-party content
sections.body: Advertisements and storefront content belong to their owners. They are displayed for analysis; you are responsible for creating original materials.

sections.title: 5. Subscriptions
sections.body: Paid plans renew automatically until cancelled. Limits for each plan are stated on the pricing page. Fees are non-refundable except where required by law.

sections.title: 6. Liability
sections.body: To the extent permitted by law, our liability is limited to the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim.

sections.title: 7. Termination
sections.body: You may delete your account at any time. We may suspend accounts that breach these terms.
